question.title: Customer Order Totals with Product Information
question.desc: Find the total amount spent by each customer, along with their name and the name of the products they purchased, ordered by total spent in descending order.
question.setup: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS customers; CREATE TABLE customers (id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(255)); INSERT INTO customers (name) VALUES ('John'), ('Jane'), ('Bob'); DROP TABLE IF EXISTS orders; CREATE TABLE orders (id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER, product_id INTEGER, total DECIMAL(10, 2)); INSERT INTO orders (customer_id, product_id, total) VALUES (1, 1, 10.99), (1, 2, 5.99), (2, 3, 7.99), (3, 1, 10.99), (1, 1, 10.99); DROP TABLE IF EXISTS products; CREATE TABLE products (id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(255)); INSERT INTO products (name) VALUES ('Product A'), ('Product B'), ('Product C');
question.solution: WITH customer_orders AS (SELECT c.name, p.name AS product_name, o.total FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id JOIN products p ON o.product_id = p.id) SELECT name, product_name, SUM(total) AS total_spent FROM customer_orders GROUP BY name, product_name ORDER BY total_spent DESC;
question.tips: Consider using window functions for more complex aggregations.
hints: Start by joining the customers, orders, and products tables based on their relationships.
Use a Common Table Expression (CTE) to simplify the query and improve readability.
Group the results by customer name and product name, and use the SUM aggregation function to calculate the total spent.
